services.name: Recurring janitorial
services.summary: Nightly or weekly cleaning of offices, clinics and shared buildings on a contract, with the same crew each visit and a written scope.

services.name: Deep clean and floor care
services.summary: The first clean of a new site, a seasonal reset, or floor work: carpet extraction, strip and re-wax, edges and vents that a nightly visit does not reach.

services.name: Window cleaning
services.summary: Interior glass and ground-floor exterior glass, on a one-off or a quarterly schedule. Anything above the ground floor is a specialist job we subcontract.

services.name: Building maintenance
services.summary: A technician for the small jobs a building accumulates: filters, lamps, doors and closers, furniture, signage, the odd leak before it becomes a claim.

services.name: After-hours response
services.summary: A call-out within four hours for water, glass, a biohazard or a building that cannot open. Contracted clients only, at the call-out price plus the work.

services.name: Day porter
services.summary: A person on site during business hours for a lobby, a lunch room, a restroom round or a building that needs someone present.

priceBook.name: Office cleaning, one visit, up to 3,000 sq ft
priceBook.notes: The flat price for a site of 3,000 sq ft or less. A larger site is priced per square foot for the whole site, not the flat price plus extra.

priceBook.name: Office cleaning, one visit, above 3,000 sq ft
priceBook.notes: Used for the whole site when it is larger than 3,000 sq ft.

priceBook.name: Deep clean, first visit
priceBook.notes: The first deep clean at a site we do not already clean. The minimum applies to the line, not to the quote.

priceBook.name: Deep clean, returning contract client
priceBook.notes: A deep clean at a site already on a Northwind contract.

priceBook.name: Carpet extraction
priceBook.notes: Two passes with a pre-spray. A third pass for a badly soiled area is a second line at the same rate.

priceBook.name: Strip and re-wax resilient flooring
priceBook.notes: Includes four coats. A fifth coat is included only on a written scope.

priceBook.name: Restroom sanitising
priceBook.notes: A full sanitise: fixtures, partitions, floors and touchpoints. A nightly contract already includes it; an add-on is priced here.

priceBook.name: Restroom consumables
priceBook.notes: Soap, towels, tissue and liners, restocked on the visit. Charged per restroom per visit, on contract.

priceBook.name: Interior window cleaning
priceBook.notes: Glass, frame and sill, reachable from the floor with a pole or a step ladder.

priceBook.name: Exterior window cleaning, ground floor
priceBook.notes: Ground floor only. Anything above it is a subcontract and a person's quote.

priceBook.name: Day porter
priceBook.notes: Business hours, four-hour minimum per visit is a scheduling rule and is applied by operations, not by the price book.

priceBook.name: Maintenance technician
priceBook.notes: Business hours, parts at cost plus handling. Materials are never estimated on a quote; the technician lists them on the invoice.

priceBook.name: After-hours call-out, first hour
priceBook.notes: Includes the first hour on site and travel. Further time is the maintenance technician rate.

priceBook.name: HVAC filter change
priceBook.notes: Standard filter, one per unit. A non-standard filter is a parts line and a person's quote.

priceBook.name: Lamp and ballast replacement
priceBook.notes: Labour and a standard lamp. A ballast or a fitting is a parts line on the invoice.

priceBook.name: Door, lock and closer repair
priceBook.notes: Two-hour minimum, because the technician cannot leave a door that will not secure.

priceBook.name: Entry mat service
priceBook.notes: A laundered mat swapped on the visit, per mat per month.

refunds.summary: A complaint is answered the same business day, a re-clean is offered when the work fell short, a credit note is Eileen's, and money back is Dana's. A refund is never agreed at the counter or in an email by anyone else.

discounts.summary: A person approves every discount, however small. The ladder is what Marcus usually agrees to for a longer commitment; it is a habit, not a permission.

safety: Nobody cleans above the ground floor on a ladder; anything that needs a lift, a rope or a roof is subcontracted to a specialist with its own insurance.
Chemicals are never decanted into unlabelled bottles and never mixed. A site's chemical list is in its binder.
A lone worker checks in at the start and the end of a visit. A missed check-in is a phone call, then Priya.
An injury, a near miss, damaged property or a break-in is reported to Priya within the hour and written up the same day, whatever the size of it.
A client's alarm code, key or access card is never written in an email, a chat or a quote.
dataHandling: Client contacts, keys, codes and site notes live in the operations system, not in an inbox.
No card number, bank detail or tax identifier is ever written into a quote, a note or a message.
A request for a client's data, a deletion or an export goes to Dana; nobody answers it alone.
Client documents are shared by link with access named, never attached to a message that leaves the company.
commitments: A start date is operations' to give. A quote never carries one.
A price is quoted from the price book or not at all; there is no 'about' and no rounding up.
A discount is never described as agreed until a person has agreed it.
A re-clean, a credit or a refund is never promised on the spot; the person who owns it decides.
Insurance certificates and contract terms come from Dana, not from a quote.
We never take on work outside the service area, and never promise a crew size.

tone.summary: Plain, warm and specific. Short sentences, the client's own words for their building, and one clear next step. Confident about what we do well, honest about what we do not do.
always: Name the person who decides, and how to reach them.
Use the client's name for the site, not 'your facility'.
Say what a price includes, and what it does not.
Answer the question that was asked before adding anything.
never: Claims about results we have not measured.
A promise the price book and the policies do not support.
An apology that admits fault before a person has looked at the visit.

ticketRoutes.when: A credit, refund or invoice dispute an agent hands on: Finance and Billing owns disputes and credit notes, and passes a refund to the person who decides money back.

escalation.when: Any discount, any size, including one the ladder would normally cover.
A quote whose lines come to more than the quote limit.
A non-standard term: a penalty clause, a short termination window, insurance above ours, or a name on the contract that is not the site.
A client says a visit was missed, short or badly done.
A client disputes an invoice, asks for a credit, or wants to change payment terms.
A client asks for money returned rather than a credit.
A client wants a firm start date, a crew size, or a change to the schedule.
An injury, a near miss, damage or a break-in at any site.
A client wants a different product, a machine, or a consumable we do not stock.
Anything about a person's job, pay, hours or leave.
A client asks about data, an audit, a background check or a security questionnaire.

glossary.meaning: A written agreement for a set scope at a set frequency, invoiced monthly, with a notice period on both sides.
One attendance at one site. A nightly contract of five nights a week is about 21.65 visits in a standard month, because a month is 4.33 weeks.
The written list of what a visit covers and what it does not. A price without a scope is not a quote.
A 30-minute site visit with a client before quoting, so the square footage and the condition are seen rather than guessed. Operations books it.
The folder at the site with the scope, the chemical list, the alarm instructions and the checklist.
A return visit to put right work that fell short, at no charge, within the re-clean window. Tom decides whether one is owed.
A reduction on an invoice, issued by Eileen. It is not money back.
An after-hours attendance for a problem that cannot wait until the next scheduled visit.
A person on site during business hours rather than after them.
The cleaner who signs off a visit and carries the site binder. Not a supervisor, and not someone who agrees a price.
Soap, towels, tissue and liners. Priced per restroom per visit, never absorbed into a cleaning line.
Certificate of insurance. Dana issues one; a quote never stands in for it.
Master services agreement, the contract a recurring client signs. Dana owns the wording.

approvedClaims: Northwind Facilities has cleaned and maintained Portland buildings since 2011.
Northwind is licensed in Oregon (CCB #204118) and carries general liability, commercial auto and umbrella insurance.
Northwind serves the Portland metro within about 30 miles of downtown, including Clark County in Washington.
The office is open Monday to Friday, 07:00 to 17:00, and contracted clients reach an on-call supervisor 24 hours a day.
Northwind looks after about 90 buildings on recurring contracts.
